title: Reducedness is invariant under changing the scalar algebra by an algebra equivalence
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $A$ be a commutative $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], let $L$ and $M$ be fields equipped with $k$-algebra structures, and let $e:L\to M$ be a bijective $k$-algebra homomorphism. Then $A\otimes_k L$ is reduced if and only if $A\otimes_k M$ is reduced.

source.place: Tensor-product transport along an algebra equivalence, Tags 00CX and 05G3

proof.text: Promote the bijective k-algebra homomorphism e to the algebra equivalence AlgEquiv.ofBijective e he (Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Equiv.lean). Its inverse is a k-algebra map in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]; the equivalence records both inverse identities.

Apply Algebra.TensorProduct.congr to the identity algebra equivalence on A and the equivalence of L with M. This constructs E : $A\otimes_k L$ ≃ₐ[k] $A\otimes_k M$ using the algebra tensor maps of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. The forward map sends $a\otimes l$ to $a\otimes e(l)$, and its inverse uses the inverse scalar map.

source.place: Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), proof: the universal property Hom(A tensor_R B,C)=Hom(A,C) x_Hom(R,C) Hom(B,C); algebra.tex Tags 00CX and 05G3

proof.text: The construction Algebra.TensorProduct.congr verifies the two inverse identities by tensor extensionality: on pure tensors they are the inverse identities of the two factor equivalences. Pure tensors generate by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Thus E and E.symm are injective.

Assume $A\otimes_k L$ is reduced. Apply Mathlib isReduced_of_injective to E.symm and its injectivity. Explicitly a nilpotent y maps to a nilpotent E.symm(y), which is zero in the reduced source tensor product. Injectivity then gives y = 0, proving reducedness of $A\otimes_k M$.

Conversely assume $A\otimes_k M$ is reduced. Apply Mathlib isReduced_of_injective to E and its injectivity. A nilpotent x maps to zero, and injectivity gives x = 0. The two implications give the required equivalence.
